tagline: The southernmost point of mainland Australia, with beaches, tracks and wombats
description: Wilsons Promontory, known as the Prom, is a national park of about 50,000 hectares in South Gippsland, 224 km from Melbourne. About 130 km of walking trails lead to granite headlands, bays and the southernmost lighthouse on the mainland. Tidal River is the hub, with a store, visitor centre and campsites, and its wombats, kangaroos and emus are used to people. The promontory has been a national park in one form or another since 1898, on the traditional country of the Gunaikurnai and Boon Wurrung peoples.
whyVisit: Walk coastal tracks to the southern tip
Watch wombats, kangaroos and emus up close
Swim and relax on white-sand beaches
Snorkel or dive in the marine parks

goodToKnow.title: Book camping early
goodToKnow.detail: Tidal River has 480 unpowered sites. Bookings are essential for Christmas, January and popular long weekends.

goodToKnow.title: Drive carefully at dusk
goodToKnow.detail: Animals are on the road around sunset and at night, especially on the 30 km from the entrance to Tidal River.

goodToKnow.title: Fuel up before the park
goodToKnow.detail: Tidal River no longer sells fuel and its store has inflated prices. The nearest petrol station is at Yanakie.

bestTimeBlurb: Go in {months} for warm swimming and camping. March is quieter than the Christmas and January peak.

tagline: Australia's cultural capital, with Victorian architecture, galleries and trams
description: Melbourne, known as Naarm in Woiworrung, is Australia's second-biggest city, home to about 5.4 million people. It is noted for Victorian-era architecture, museums, galleries, theatres, parks and gardens, and for a strong food, wine and coffee culture and live music scene. Australian rules football was invented here, and the World Heritage-listed Royal Exhibition Building and the Melbourne Cricket Ground are landmarks. It is also the usual base for the Great Ocean Road, the Grampians and Phillip Island's penguin parade.
whyVisit: Wander laneways for street art and coffee
Eat through the city's migrant cuisines

goodToKnow.title: Free Tram Zone
goodToKnow.detail: Trams in the CBD Free Tram Zone cost nothing and need no touch-on. Touching on inside it charges a full fare.

goodToKnow.title: Pack for any weather
goodToKnow.detail: The weather can swing through four seasons in a day, so carry a layer and a rain jacket even in summer.

goodToKnow.title: Get a myki card
goodToKnow.detail: Trains, trams and buses use the myki card (adult card $6). Daily fares are capped, at $11.00 on weekdays as of Mar 2025.

bestTimeBlurb: {months} brings mild days for exploring on foot. Summer can be hot and winters cool and damp.
